intent.raw_query: Cambodia Angkor Wat + beaches, $1100, 10 days, November 2026

selected_hotel.name: Angkor Archaeological Park, Siem Reap Boutique Stay

experiences.name: Angkor Wat Sunrise Tour
experiences.description: Witness the breathtaking sunrise over the iconic Angkor Wat temple complex, one of the world's greatest archaeological wonders. Explore the intricate bas-reliefs and towering spires that tell the story of the ancient Khmer Empire, guided by a local historian.

experiences.name: Koh Rong Beachfront Snorkeling
experiences.description: Explore the crystal-clear turquoise waters surrounding Koh Rong island with a guided snorkeling excursion. Discover vibrant coral reefs, tropical fish, and stunning marine biodiversity just steps from the white sandy beachfront shores.

experiences.name: Sihanoukville Street Food & Seafood Night Market
experiences.description: Stroll through the vibrant beachfront night market sampling authentic Cambodian street food including fresh grilled seafood, Lok Lak beef, Amok fish curry, and tropical fruit shakes. Engage with local vendors and learn about Khmer culinary traditions.

experiences.name: Ream National Park Cultural & Nature Walk
experiences.description: Join a guided eco-cultural walk through Ream National Park, where you can visit traditional fishing villages, learn about the coastal Khmer way of life, explore mangrove forests, and spot rare wildlife including dolphins and sea eagles along the beachfront coastline.
experiences.location: Ream National Park, Preah Sihanouk Province

experiences.name: Koh Rong Samloem Sunset Kayaking
experiences.description: Paddle through the calm, glassy waters surrounding Koh Rong Samloem island during golden hour. Explore hidden sea caves, secluded lagoons, and pristine beachfront coves while learning about the island's history and local fishing culture from your guide.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Cambodia
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

hotel.name: Angkor Archaeological Park, Siem Reap Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 13:00
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Siem Reap International Airport at 13:00. Clear immigration and collect baggage. Take a tuk-tuk to your boutique stay near Angkor Archaeological Park (approx. $5–7 USD). Check in, freshen up, and take a slow walk around the immediate hotel surroundings to orient yourself. Visit the nearby Angkor Night Market area to get a feel for the town.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along Pub Street and the Old Market (Psah Chas) area. Browse local souvenir stalls and enjoy the lively atmosphere. Watch a free Apsara dance performance preview outside local restaurants.

meals.breakfast: Eaten on the plane or at the airport
meals.lunch: Grab a quick and affordable meal at the airport or a local noodle stall near the hotel on arrival (~$2–3 USD)
meals.dinner: Dinner at Khmer Kitchen Restaurant near Pub Street — try Amok fish curry and jasmine rice (~$4–6 USD per person)

day_by_day.notes: Exchange a small amount of USD at the airport or use ATMs in town. Cambodia widely accepts USD. Negotiate tuk-tuk fares before boarding. Stay hydrated as November can still be warm and humid.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up early (4:30 AM) for the iconic Angkor Wat sunrise. Purchase a 3-day Angkor Pass ($62 USD — best value for your stay). Watch the sun rise over the iconic towers reflecting in the lotus pond. Explore the outer galleries of Angkor Wat, including the famous bas-relief carvings depicting the Churning of the Ocean of Milk and the Ramayana epic.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring the inner sanctum and upper levels of Angkor Wat. Walk or hire a tuk-tuk ($15–20 USD for a full-day driver) to nearby Angkor Thom complex. Visit the Bayon Temple with its 216 serene stone faces, then explore the Baphuon and the Terrace of the Elephants.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Siem Reap town. Visit Angkor Night Market for cheap local handicrafts and souvenirs. Enjoy a $1 draft beer at a local bar.

meals.breakfast: Skip or grab a banana and coffee from a street vendor near Angkor Wat (~$1 USD)
meals.lunch: Pack snacks or eat at one of the affordable food stalls inside the Angkor complex (~$2–3 USD for rice and grilled meat)
meals.dinner: Try Marum Restaurant (social enterprise, affordable) or a local Khmer BBQ buffet on Pub Street (~$5–8 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Bring sunscreen, a hat, and at least 1.5 liters of water. Wear comfortable shoes as you'll be walking on uneven stone surfaces. Dress modestly — shoulders and knees must be covered to enter temple sanctuaries.

day_by_day.morning: Use your Angkor Pass to visit Ta Prohm — the famous 'Tomb Raider' temple dramatically engulfed by massive tree roots. Arrive early (7:00–8:00 AM) before tour groups arrive. Spend time photographing the surreal jungle-temple atmosphere and reading about the Jayavarman VII era history.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Preah Khan Temple, a sprawling complex with long corridors and intricate carvings, often less crowded than Angkor Wat. Afterward, explore Neak Pean, a unique artificial island temple, and Ta Som, a smaller but beautifully atmospheric temple with a tree-covered eastern gopura.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the Siem Reap Artisans d'Angkor workshop (free entry) to see local craftspeople carving stone and silk-weaving — a great cultural insight. Browse their affordable gift shop.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your hotel or a local bakery — try Khmer red rice porridge (Bobor) from a street stall (~$1.50 USD)
meals.lunch: Eat at a local food stall near Ta Prohm — grilled corn, rice dishes, and fresh coconut water (~$3 USD total)
meals.dinner: Dinner at Psar Chaa (Old Market) food court — multiple Khmer dishes to choose from at very low prices (~$3–5 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Ta Prohm is extremely popular — arriving before 8:00 AM makes a significant difference in crowd levels. Hire the same tuk-tuk driver from Day 2 if possible for continuity and a better rate.

day_by_day.morning: Use your final day of the Angkor Pass to visit the remote Banteay Srei temple (approx. 25 km from Siem Reap). Known as the 'Jewel of Khmer Art,' it features extraordinarily detailed pink sandstone carvings. Hire your tuk-tuk driver for a half-day trip (~$12–15 USD). En route, stop at the Landmine Museum to learn about Cambodia's painful recent history (entry ~$5 USD).
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Siem Reap and visit the Angkor National Museum ($12 USD entry) to deepen your understanding of Khmer history, religion, and the civilization that built Angkor. Well worth the cost for history enthusiasts.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a traditional Khmer cooking class for budget travelers — several guesthouses and local schools offer 2-hour classes for $10–15 USD including a market visit. Learn to cook Amok, Lok Lak, and Khmer green mango salad.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at a local café — Khmer baguette sandwich with pâté and iced coffee (~$2 USD, a French-Khmer fusion legacy)
meals.lunch: Pack snacks for the Banteay Srei trip or eat at a roadside stall near the temple (~$2–3 USD)
meals.dinner: Eat what you cooked in the cooking class, or head to a local restaurant for Lok Lak (stir-fried beef with rice) (~$4–5 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Banteay Srei requires your Angkor Pass. The road can be dusty — bring a scarf or mask. The Landmine Museum is sobering but highly recommended for cultural context about modern Cambodian history.

day_by_day.morning: Travel day: Take an early morning bus from Siem Reap to Phnom Penh (approx. 6 hours, $8–12 USD with Giant Ibis or Mekong Express — book in advance). Depart around 7:00–8:00 AM. Enjoy the countryside scenery along National Road 6.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Phnom Penh around 1:00–2:00 PM. Check into a budget guesthouse near the riverside (dorms from $5, private rooms from $12–18 USD). Take a walk along the Sisowath Quay riverside promenade and visit the Royal Palace grounds from the outside.
day_by_day.evening: Visit the Royal Palace and Silver Pagoda (open until 5:00 PM, $10 USD entry) if you arrive early enough, or save it for tomorrow morning. Walk the lively riverfront and watch the sunset over the Tonlé Sap and Mekong river confluence.

meals.breakfast: Quick breakfast before departure — Khmer noodle soup (Kuy Teav) from a street stall (~$1.50 USD)
meals.lunch: Eat on the bus or grab food at a rest stop along the highway (~$2–3 USD)
meals.dinner: Dinner at a local Cambodian restaurant near the riverside — try Khmer fish soup or rice with vegetables (~$3–5 USD). FCC (Foreign Correspondents' Club) has affordable happy hour drinks with great river views.

day_by_day.notes: Book bus tickets at least a day in advance. Giant Ibis is the most reliable budget bus company with good safety records. Store valuables securely during the bus journey. Phnom Penh is more urban — be more cautious with bag snatching near the riverside.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Tuol Sleng Genocide Museum (S-21 Prison, $8 USD entry with audio guide). This former high school turned Khmer Rouge prison is one of the most important historical sites in Southeast Asia. Allow 2–3 hours for a thorough and respectful visit. A deeply moving and essential experience for understanding modern Cambodia.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Choeung Ek Genocidal Center (Killing Fields), located about 15 km from the city center (tuk-tuk ~$8–10 USD round trip, entry $6 USD including audio guide). The audio guide narrated by survivors is extraordinarily powerful. Allow 2 hours.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the city center. Visit the Russian Market (Psar Toul Tom Poung) for affordable local goods, clothing, and souvenirs. Bargain confidently — start at 50% of the asking price.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at a local café near your guesthouse — French-style baguette with eggs and coffee (~$2 USD)
meals.lunch: Eat near Tuol Sleng at a local Khmer restaurant — rice with multiple side dishes (Bai Sach Chrouk, pork and rice) (~$2–3 USD)
meals.dinner: Dinner at a local restaurant near the Russian Market or riverside — try grilled fish with Khmer herbs (~$4–6 USD). Street food like grilled skewers available for $0.50–1 USD each.

day_by_day.notes: The Tuol Sleng and Killing Fields visits are emotionally heavy. Take your time, be respectful, and dress modestly. These sites are crucial to understanding Cambodia's resilience. Avoid visiting both in one day if you feel overwhelmed — you can split them.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Royal Palace and Silver Pagoda ($10 USD entry). Admire the Throne Hall, the Moonlight Pavilion, and the Silver Pagoda floor made of 5,000 silver tiles. See the Emerald Buddha and a replica of the famous Khmer Emerald Buddha. Walk through beautifully manicured gardens.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the National Museum of Cambodia ($10 USD entry) — an excellent collection of Khmer art and sculpture spanning 1,000 years, including pieces from Angkor. Then walk to the Central Market (Psar Thmei) — a stunning Art Deco building from 1937 — for local shopping and people-watching.
day_by_day.evening: Take an optional sunset cruise on the Mekong River ($8–12 USD for a 1-hour boat tour departing from the riverside). Watch the sun set over the river confluence while sipping a local Angkor beer.

meals.breakfast: Visit Phnom Penh's famous local market for Nom Banh Chok (Khmer noodles with fish-based green curry sauce) — a traditional breakfast (~$1.50 USD)
meals.lunch: Lunch near the National Museum — try a local Banh Mi sandwich shop (~$1.50–2 USD) or a restaurant with a set lunch menu (~$4 USD)
meals.dinner: Dinner at Romdeng Restaurant (social enterprise training former street youth in hospitality, moderately priced ~$6–10 USD) — try deep-fried tarantulas if adventurous, or stick to excellent Khmer classics

day_by_day.notes: Sunday mornings are lively at the riverside — locals gather for exercise and markets. The Royal Palace is closed on public holidays. Check the schedule in advance. Modest dress required for the Royal Palace.

day_by_day.morning: Travel day: Take an early morning bus or minivan from Phnom Penh to Sihanoukville (approx. 4–5 hours, $6–10 USD). Alternatively, take a bus to Kampot (~3 hours, $6 USD) for a more relaxed beach-adjacent experience. For beaches, head to Sihanoukville and take a boat to Koh Rong Samloem island (~$25 USD round trip boat). Check into a budget beach bungalow ($15–25 USD/night).
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Koh Rong Samloem and check into your beach accommodation. Spend the afternoon relaxing on the pristine white sand beaches of Saracen Bay or M'Pai Bay. The water in November is warm and calm — ideal for swimming.
day_by_day.evening: Watch the spectacular bioluminescent plankton light up the water after dark (best seen by swimming or kayaking at night — ask your guesthouse for the best spots). This natural phenomenon is one of Cambodia's most magical experiences.

meals.breakfast: Eat before departing Phnom Penh — grab a local breakfast near your guesthouse (~$1.50–2 USD)
meals.lunch: Eat at a rest stop on the bus journey or grab food in Sihanoukville port before boarding the boat (~$3–4 USD)
meals.dinner: Fresh seafood BBQ dinner at a beachside restaurant on Koh Rong Samloem — grilled fish, prawns, and rice (~$6–10 USD)

day_by_day.notes: Book your boat ticket to Koh Rong Samloem in advance during peak season (November is peak season). Speed boats run several times daily from Sihanoukville. Bring cash as ATMs are limited on the island. Pack insect repellent.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up early and walk to the quieter side of the island (M'Pai Bay if staying in Saracen Bay, or vice versa) along jungle trails. Enjoy the pristine, uncrowded beaches. Swim, snorkel (rent equipment for ~$5 USD/day), and spot colorful reef fish in the crystal-clear water.
day_by_day.afternoon: Join an affordable snorkeling day trip from the island ($15–20 USD) to nearby coral reefs and uninhabited islands. Alternatively, rent a kayak (~$5–8 USD/half day) and paddle along the coastline exploring hidden coves and lagoons. Enjoy a hammock afternoon on the beach.
day_by_day.evening: Socialize with fellow travelers at your beach bungalow or a beachside bar. Enjoy a bonfire on the beach if organized by your guesthouse. Look for bioluminescence again in the shallows — it's truly unmissable.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your guesthouse — fruit plate, toast, and eggs (~$3–4 USD)
meals.lunch: Beach barbecue or a simple rice and fish lunch at a local beach shack (~$4–5 USD). Fresh coconuts available for ~$1 USD.
meals.dinner: Dinner at a beachside restaurant — try whole grilled barracuda or squid with garlic and butter (~$7–10 USD). Sunset cocktails from $2–3 USD.

day_by_day.notes: November is generally calm and sunny on Cambodia's southern coast, making it an ideal time to visit. Bring reef-safe sunscreen to protect the coral. There are limited medical facilities on the island — bring a basic first aid kit.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning — enjoy one last sunrise on the beach. Take a slow morning swim and soak in the last moments of island paradise. Pack up and check out of your bungalow. Take the morning boat back to Sihanoukville.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on your departure flight, spend time in Sihanoukville or travel back to Phnom Penh (buses run frequently, ~$6–10 USD, 4–5 hours). If time permits, visit Otres Beach near Sihanoukville for a final beach walk. Buy last-minute souvenirs at local markets — Kampot pepper, silk scarves, and carved wooden items make great budget gifts.
day_by_day.evening: Final dinner in Cambodia — treat yourself to a slightly nicer Khmer meal to celebrate the end of a wonderful trip. Reflect on the incredible history, culture, and natural beauty experienced over 10 days. Head to the airport or your final accommodation for departure.

meals.breakfast: Final Cambodian breakfast on the island — fresh fruit smoothie and toast (~$2–3 USD)
meals.lunch: Quick lunch in Sihanoukville or on the road — Banh Mi sandwich or rice dish (~$2–3 USD)
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at a quality Khmer restaurant in Phnom Penh or Sihanoukville — splurge slightly on your last night for a memorable meal (~$8–12 USD). Try Khmer red curry or grilled Mekong river fish.

day_by_day.notes: Confirm your return transport and flight details the night before. Keep some USD cash for airport taxes or last-minute expenses. Cambodia charges a $25 USD departure tax (usually included in international flight tickets — verify with your airline). Leave a tip for your tuk-tuk drivers and guesthouse staff — it's greatly appreciated.

trip_options.title: Classic Cambodia Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

hotel.name: Angkor Archaeological Park, Siem Reap Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Siem Reap International Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Rest and transit time.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check in to your Boutique Stay near Angkor Archaeological Park. After freshening up, take a leisurely stroll around the hotel grounds and nearby Angkor village area to orient yourself. Visit the nearby Angkor National Museum (entry ~$12 USD) for a rich introduction to Khmer history and the Angkor civilization — perfect for setting the context before temple visits.
day_by_day.evening: Head into Siem Reap's Old Market (Phsar Chas) area for a gentle first evening. Explore Pub Street and the surrounding lanes, browse local handicraft stalls, and soak in the atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable — in-flight or airport meal on arrival day.
meals.lunch: Light meal at the hotel or a nearby café such as Blue Pumpkin Siem Reap — known for fresh sandwiches, smoothies, and pastries at mid-range prices (~$5–8 USD).
meals.dinner: Dinner at Mahob Restaurant on Pub Street — a well-regarded spot serving authentic Khmer cuisine like fish amok and beef lok lak in a comfortable setting (~$10–15 USD per person).

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light. Jet lag may be a factor. Exchange currency at the airport or a licensed money changer in town — USD is widely accepted in Cambodia. Tuk-tuk from airport to hotel costs approximately $8–12 USD.

day_by_day.morning: Rise early (5:30 AM) for the iconic sunrise at Angkor Wat. Watch the temple's reflection shimmer in the reflecting pool as the sun rises over its towers — one of the world's most breathtaking sights. Spend the morning exploring Angkor Wat's outer galleries, bas-reliefs depicting the Churning of the Ocean of Milk, and inner sanctum. Purchase a 3-day Angkor Pass (~$62 USD) for best value across multiple days.
day_by_day.afternoon: After a mid-morning break, continue to Angkor Thom — the great walled city. Visit the Bayon Temple with its 216 serene stone faces, the Baphuon, the Elephant Terrace, and the Terrace of the Leper King. Hire a knowledgeable local guide at the gate (~$25–35 USD/day) to enrich the historical context.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Siem Reap for a traditional Apsara dance performance dinner at Koulen II Restaurant or Angkor Village Theatre — a beautiful cultural experience featuring classical Khmer dance with a set dinner (~$20–25 USD).

meals.breakfast: Early light breakfast at the hotel before sunrise — pack a snack or energy bar for the temple visit.
meals.lunch: Lunch at one of the open-air restaurants near the Angkor Thom South Gate, such as Angkor Café — simple Khmer noodle soups and rice dishes (~$5–8 USD).
meals.dinner: Apsara dinner show at Koulen II or similar venue (~$20–25 USD including show and set menu).

day_by_day.notes: Wear light, breathable clothing and bring a hat, sunscreen, and plenty of water. November temperatures are pleasant (~25–30°C) with low humidity in the dry season. Modest dress required — shoulders and knees must be covered at all temples.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Ta Prohm — the famous 'jungle temple' made iconic by the Tomb Raider film, where massive silk-cotton and strangler fig trees have grown through and around the ancient stone structures. Arrive early to beat the crowds. Then visit Banteay Kdei and the tranquil Srah Srang reservoir nearby.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Banteay Srei Temple (~35 km north of Siem Reap), renowned for its exquisitely detailed pink sandstone carvings — considered the finest decorative stonework in all of Angkor. The craftsmanship is extraordinary and not to be missed. En route, stop at the Landmine Museum to learn about Cambodia's difficult recent history with UXOs and the ongoing humanitarian work.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Siem Reap. Visit the vibrant Night Market along the river for souvenir shopping — silk scarves, stone carvings, and handmade crafts. Enjoy a relaxed riverside evening.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel or at a local bakery such as Le Tigre de Papier — French-Khmer fusion pastries and coffee (~$4–6 USD).
meals.lunch: Packed lunch or snack from a roadside stall near Banteay Srei — fresh spring rolls and grilled corn are common (~$2–4 USD).
meals.dinner: Dinner at Malis Restaurant — one of Siem Reap's finest Khmer dining experiences, celebrating traditional recipes with a modern touch (~$15–20 USD per person).

day_by_day.notes: Hire a tuk-tuk for the full day for the Banteay Srei excursion (~$20–25 USD for the day). The Landmine Museum entry is by donation. Banteay Srei is worth the extra distance — plan approximately 1.5 hours of travel time round trip.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the lesser-explored but magnificent Preah Khan temple — a sprawling monastic complex with long corridors, towering trees, and an atmospheric, partially unrestored feel. Follow with a visit to Neak Pean, a unique artificial island temple set in a large reservoir, and Ta Som temple with its beautiful eastern gopura engulfed by a fig tree.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the East Mebon and Pre Rup temples — both pyramid-style temple mountains offering great views from the upper tiers. Pre Rup is particularly beautiful in the late afternoon golden light. This completes a thorough exploration of the Angkor complex over three days.
day_by_day.evening: Treat yourself to a traditional Khmer herbal massage at one of Siem Reap's reputable wellness spas — Frangipani Spa or Bodia Spa are excellent mid-range options (~$20–30 USD for a 60-minute massage). End the evening with a quiet dinner.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel.
meals.lunch: Lunch at the Angkor area food stalls near Preah Khan — rice with grilled chicken or pork (~$3–5 USD).
meals.dinner: Dinner at Sugar Palm Restaurant — a beloved local institution serving home-style Khmer cooking in a warm, intimate atmosphere (~$10–15 USD per person).

day_by_day.notes: This is your final full day using the 3-day Angkor Pass. Pre Rup at sunset is a popular spot — arrive by 4:30 PM to secure a good vantage point on the upper terrace. Comfortable walking shoes are essential across all temple days.

day_by_day.morning: Take a morning boat trip on the Tonlé Sap Lake — Southeast Asia's largest freshwater lake and a UNESCO Biosphere Reserve. Visit the floating villages of Kampong Phluk or Chong Khneas, where entire communities live on stilted houses above the water. Learn about the unique ecosystem and the fishing culture that has sustained Cambodian life for centuries.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Siem Reap and visit the Artisans Angkor workshop and boutique at Chantiers-Ecoles — a social enterprise training disadvantaged youth in traditional Khmer arts including stone carving, lacquerwork, silk weaving, and silver smithing. Watch artisans at work and browse the high-quality fair-trade goods.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a free or low-cost community cultural event if available, or explore the Alley West area of Siem Reap — a trendy neighborhood with independent cafés, galleries, and cocktail bars popular with both travelers and locals.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel before the early boat departure.
meals.lunch: Lunch at a floating village restaurant on the Tonlé Sap — fresh river fish dishes are the specialty (~$6–10 USD).
meals.dinner: Dinner at Haven Restaurant — a social enterprise training at-risk youth in hospitality, serving excellent Western and Khmer dishes in a lovely garden setting (~$10–15 USD per person).

day_by_day.notes: Book the Tonlé Sap boat tour in advance through your hotel or a reputable agency (~$15–25 USD per person). Kampong Phluk is more scenic and less touristy than Chong Khneas but requires a slightly longer boat ride. Bring insect repellent for the lake visit.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Siem Reap by bus or private transfer to Phnom Penh — Cambodia's vibrant capital city (~5–6 hours by road or ~45 minutes by domestic flight). Book a mid-range bus with Giant Ibis or Mekong Express for a comfortable journey (~$12–15 USD). If time allows, enjoy the scenery of rural Cambodia along National Road 6.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Phnom Penh and check in to your accommodation near the riverside. Begin exploration with the Royal Palace and Silver Pagoda — the official residence of the King of Cambodia. The complex features stunning Khmer and French colonial architecture, and the Silver Pagoda houses priceless Buddhist artifacts including a life-size gold Buddha encrusted with diamonds.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along the Sisowath Quay riverside promenade at golden hour — a lively boulevard lined with restaurants, bars, and cafés. Watch the sun set over the Tonlé Sap and Mekong rivers confluence.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel in Siem Reap before departure.
meals.lunch: Lunch on the bus or at a roadside stop en route — local Khmer rice dishes (~$3–5 USD).
meals.dinner: Dinner at Romdeng Restaurant in Phnom Penh — a social enterprise serving traditional Cambodian cuisine including the famous deep-fried tarantulas for the adventurous, in a beautiful colonial villa setting (~$12–18 USD per person).

day_by_day.notes: Giant Ibis is highly recommended for inter-city bus travel in Cambodia — comfortable, punctual, and with onboard snacks. Book tickets at least a day in advance. Alternatively, a private taxi costs ~$60–80 USD and is faster. Phnom Penh accommodation should be booked separately for 2 nights.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Tuol Sleng Genocide Museum (S-21 Prison) — a sobering but essential experience to understand Cambodia's tragic history under the Khmer Rouge regime (1975–1979). The former school-turned-prison now serves as a powerful memorial and museum. Audio guides are available and highly recommended (~$3 USD entry, ~$6 USD audio guide).
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Choeung Ek Killing Fields Memorial (~15 km from city center) — another deeply moving site with a Buddhist stupa containing the skulls of victims and informative audio tour. Take time to reflect. Afterward, visit the National Museum of Cambodia near the Royal Palace — housing the world's finest collection of Khmer sculpture and artifacts.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Central Market (Phsar Thmei) — a stunning Art Deco building from 1937 with a distinctive yellow dome. Browse local goods, jewelry, and souvenirs. End the evening with dinner and people-watching along the riverside.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at a riverside café such as Java Café — good coffee, eggs, and fresh fruit (~$5–8 USD).
meals.lunch: Lunch at a local restaurant near Tuol Sleng — simple Khmer noodle soup or rice dishes (~$4–6 USD).
meals.dinner: Dinner at Khmer Surin Restaurant — a popular Phnom Penh institution serving refined Khmer cuisine with Thai influences in a beautiful wooden house (~$12–18 USD per person).

day_by_day.notes: The Tuol Sleng and Choeung Ek visits are emotionally heavy — allow yourself time to process. These are among the most important historical sites in Southeast Asia and provide crucial context for understanding modern Cambodia. Dress modestly and respectfully. Tuk-tuk to Choeung Ek costs ~$10–12 USD round trip.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Phnom Penh by bus or private transfer to Sihanoukville (~3.5–4 hours), then take a ferry to Koh Rong Samloem — one of Cambodia's most beautiful and relatively unspoiled islands. The island offers pristine white sand beaches, clear turquoise water, and a relaxed atmosphere. Check in to a mid-range beachfront bungalow on Saracen Bay.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the afternoon unwinding on Saracen Bay beach — one of the most beautiful beaches in Southeast Asia. Swim in the warm, calm waters, snorkel among colorful reef fish, or simply relax in a hammock under the palm trees. Rent a kayak (~$5–8 USD/hour) to explore the coastline.
day_by_day.evening: Experience the magical bioluminescent plankton that illuminates the waters around Koh Rong Samloem after dark — wade into the shallow water at night and watch the water glow electric blue with every movement. This natural phenomenon is at its most vivid in the dry season (November is ideal).

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel in Phnom Penh before departure.
meals.lunch: Lunch at a beachside shack on Saracen Bay after arrival — fresh grilled fish, coconut rice, and cold drinks (~$6–10 USD).
meals.dinner: Dinner at one of the beachfront restaurants on Saracen Bay — fresh seafood barbecue platter with rice and vegetables, enjoyed with your feet in the sand (~$10–15 USD per person).

day_by_day.notes: Ferries from Sihanoukville to Koh Rong Samloem depart multiple times daily — book in advance during peak season. Speed boat takes ~45 minutes (~$25–30 USD round trip). There are no ATMs on the island — bring sufficient cash. The bioluminescence is best seen on moonless nights; check lunar calendar.

day_by_day.morning: Take a guided snorkeling or diving trip around the marine park surrounding Koh Rong Samloem. The coral reefs host diverse marine life including reef sharks, sea turtles, and colorful tropical fish. Several dive operators on the island offer PADI discover dives for beginners (~$35–45 USD) or guided snorkel tours (~$15–20 USD).
day_by_day.afternoon: Hike across the island to the secluded Lazy Beach on the western side — a hidden gem with even fewer visitors, dramatic scenery, and excellent swimming. The jungle trail takes approximately 45 minutes each way through lush tropical forest. Alternatively, hire a boat taxi (~$5–10 USD) for a quicker crossing.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Saracen Bay for a relaxed final island evening. Watch the sunset paint the sky over the Gulf of Thailand. Join fellow travelers at a beachside bar for sundowners — fresh coconuts, tropical cocktails, and good conversation.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your bungalow or a beachside café — tropical fruit platter, eggs, and fresh juice (~$4–7 USD).
meals.lunch: Packed lunch from your accommodation for the Lazy Beach hike, or snacks purchased from a small shop near the trail.
meals.dinner: Farewell island dinner at a slightly more elevated beachfront restaurant — try Cambodian-style steamed fish with lemongrass and ginger, accompanied by a sunset view (~$12–18 USD per person).

day_by_day.notes: Apply reef-safe sunscreen only when snorkeling to protect the marine ecosystem. Wear sturdy shoes for the jungle hike to Lazy Beach. Stay hydrated — the trail can be warm and humid. Book your return ferry for the following morning in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning on Koh Rong Samloem — take an early sunrise walk along the empty beach, do a final swim, or simply enjoy a peaceful breakfast watching the fishing boats head out. Take the morning ferry back to Sihanoukville and transfer to Phnom Penh airport or Sihanoukville airport for your departure flight.
day_by_day.afternoon: If your departure flight allows, spend a couple of hours at Sihanoukville before heading to the airport — the town itself has limited charm but the Victory Beach area has decent cafés for a final Cambodian coffee and meal. Alternatively, if flying from Phnom Penh, use the transfer time to pick up any last-minute souvenirs at the airport shops.
day_by_day.evening: Departure — carry with you the memories of ancient temples, floating villages, sobering history, vibrant culture, and paradise beaches. Cambodia's warmth, resilience, and extraordinary heritage make it one of Southeast Asia's most rewarding destinations.

meals.breakfast: Final breakfast on the island — enjoy fresh tropical fruit, local coffee, and a leisurely meal before the ferry (~$4–7 USD).
meals.lunch: Lunch at a restaurant in Sihanoukville or at the airport — Khmer fried rice or noodle soup for a final taste of Cambodia (~$5–8 USD).
meals.dinner: In-flight meal or airport dining depending on departure schedule.

day_by_day.notes: Allow ample time for the ferry + transfer to the airport — the total journey from Koh Rong Samloem to Phnom Penh airport takes approximately 5–6 hours including ferry, road transfer, and check-in. Plan your departure flight no earlier than early evening if flying from Phnom Penh. Pack a small day bag for easy access during transit. Declare any purchased artifacts or antiques at customs.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Cambodia Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

hotel.name: Angkor Archaeological Park, Siem Reap Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Siem Reap International Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Private luxury transfer arranged to boutique stay within Angkor Archaeological Park.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check-in and settle into your boutique property. Enjoy a welcome drink and orientation briefing with your dedicated concierge. Take a leisurely stroll through the hotel gardens to acclimatize. Optional: a relaxing dip in the pool or a 60-minute Khmer herbal welcome massage at the in-house spa.
day_by_day.evening: Private sunset tuk-tuk ride to the Angkor Archaeological Park's outer perimeter for a golden-hour view of Angkor Wat's iconic silhouette reflecting in the moat — a breathtaking first impression. Return to the hotel for a curated welcome dinner.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable (in-flight or post-arrival light snack at hotel)
meals.lunch: Welcome light lunch platter served poolside at the boutique hotel upon arrival
meals.dinner: Private candlelit dinner at the hotel's signature restaurant featuring Khmer Royal Cuisine — try amok trey (fish amok) and lok lak beef with jasmine rice

day_by_day.notes: Ensure passports and e-visas are ready before landing. Arrange SIM card or international data plan at the airport. November weather in Siem Reap is ideal — cool, dry season just beginning, temperatures around 25–30°C.

day_by_day.morning: Pre-dawn rise for an exclusive sunrise experience at Angkor Wat (entry by 5:15 AM). Watch the sun rise behind the five lotus-shaped towers reflected in the sacred ponds — one of the world's most iconic vistas. Accompanied by a private expert archaeologist guide who will narrate the temple's 12th-century Khmer history and Hindu-Buddhist iconography.
day_by_day.afternoon: Guided exploration of Angkor Wat's inner sanctum, bas-relief galleries (depicting the Churning of the Ocean of Milk and the Battle of Kurukshetra), and the central tower. After the temple, enjoy a private lunch at a nearby heritage restaurant before visiting the South Gate of Angkor Thom and the enigmatic Bayon Temple with its 216 serene stone faces.
day_by_day.evening: Visit Baphuon Temple and the Terrace of the Elephants at dusk. Return to hotel for a sunset cocktail on the terrace. Dinner at a premium Siem Reap restaurant in town.

meals.breakfast: Pre-dawn light breakfast box prepared by the hotel (fruit, pastries, coffee/tea) enjoyed at Angkor Wat
meals.lunch: Private lunch at Mahob Restaurant or The Sugar Palm — authentic Khmer cuisine in a heritage setting; try samlor kako (pork and vegetable soup)
meals.dinner: Dinner at Cuisine Wat Damnak — one of Cambodia's finest farm-to-table restaurants offering contemporary Khmer tasting menus with wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable walking shoes and light breathable clothing. Shoulders and knees must be covered inside temples. Bring sunscreen, a hat, and a reusable water bottle. Private guide and air-conditioned vehicle are essential for this full day.

day_by_day.morning: Exclusive early morning visit to Ta Prohm — the 'Tomb Raider' temple famously engulfed by giant silk-cotton and strangler fig trees. Arrive before the crowds for a mystical, atmospheric experience. Your private guide will explain the Jayavarman VII-era Buddhist monastery's history and the deliberate conservation decision to leave the trees in place.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Preah Khan Temple (a sprawling monastic complex) and Neak Pean (an artificial island temple set in a reservoir). After the temples, visit the Angkor National Museum for an in-depth multimedia journey through Khmer civilization, royal regalia, and the Angkor empire's golden age. Enjoy a private curator-led tour.
day_by_day.evening: Attend an exclusive Apsara dance performance — a UNESCO-recognized art form — at a premium venue such as Amansara or a private performance arranged at your hotel. Elegant traditional Khmer dance dinner show.

meals.breakfast: Full gourmet breakfast at the hotel — Khmer congee (bobor), tropical fruit platters, eggs to order, freshly brewed Cambodian coffee
meals.lunch: Lunch at Haven Restaurant — a social enterprise training restaurant offering excellent Khmer and Western dishes in a tranquil garden setting
meals.dinner: Traditional Khmer Royal Banquet dinner paired with Apsara performance; multi-course set menu featuring grilled river prawns, Khmer curry, and palm sugar desserts

day_by_day.notes: Ta Prohm is best visited early (before 8 AM) to avoid tour groups. The Angkor Museum requires approximately 2 hours. Dress code for the Apsara dinner show is smart casual to semi-formal.

day_by_day.morning: Private hot air balloon ride over the Angkor Archaeological Park at sunrise — a truly once-in-a-lifetime aerial perspective of the temple complex, jungle canopy, and surrounding countryside. Approximately 45–60 minutes aloft with champagne upon landing.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the remote and less-visited Banteay Srei Temple — the 'Citadel of Women' — renowned for its extraordinarily intricate pink sandstone carvings, considered the finest examples of Khmer decorative art. Located 25 km northeast of Angkor, a scenic private car journey through rural Cambodian countryside. Stop at a local village for a brief authentic cultural interaction.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset visit to Phnom Bakheng hill temple for panoramic views over the Angkor plain and Tonlé Sap Lake glimmering in the distance. Return to Siem Reap's Pub Street area for a curated evening at leisure — explore the night market or enjoy cocktails at a rooftop bar.

meals.breakfast: Light pre-flight snack provided by balloon operator; full breakfast at hotel upon return
meals.lunch: Picnic-style gourmet lunch prepared by the hotel and enjoyed in the shade near Banteay Srei — fresh baguettes, local cheeses, tropical fruits, and Cambodian iced coffee
meals.dinner: Dinner at Malis Restaurant — celebrated Cambodian chef Luu Meng's flagship fine-dining restaurant; try the seven-course Khmer Heritage tasting menu

day_by_day.notes: Hot air balloon is weather-dependent; confirm the evening before. Banteay Srei is a 40-minute drive — plan for 3–4 hours round trip including exploration. Phnom Bakheng requires advance timed tickets; your concierge should book these in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Private boat excursion on Tonlé Sap Lake — Southeast Asia's largest freshwater lake and a UNESCO Biosphere Reserve. Visit the extraordinary floating villages of Kampong Phluk, where entire communities live on stilts and wooden platforms above the water. Guided by a local expert, learn about the unique ecosystem and the lives of the lake's fishing communities.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Siem Reap. Visit Artisans Angkor — a social enterprise workshop and showroom where master craftspeople preserve traditional Khmer silk weaving, lacquerware, stone carving, and wood carving. Enjoy a private behind-the-scenes workshop tour and the opportunity to purchase premium authentic handicrafts. Optional: a silk-weaving demonstration and hands-on lesson.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at the rooftop terrace of a luxury Siem Reap hotel (FCC Angkor or Raffles Grand Hotel d'Angkor). Leisurely evening at leisure — explore the Old French Quarter on foot.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — freshly made Cambodian noodle soup (kuy teav) station alongside international buffet
meals.lunch: Lunch aboard the private boat on Tonlé Sap — fresh grilled fish caught by local fishermen, prepared simply with lime, lemongrass, and herbs
meals.dinner: Dinner at Raffles Grand Hotel d'Angkor's Le Grand restaurant — colonial elegance with an innovative menu blending French technique and Cambodian ingredients; excellent wine cellar

day_by_day.notes: Tonlé Sap water levels are ideal in November post-monsoon season — the lake is at its fullest and floating villages are most accessible. Bring insect repellent for the lake excursion. Artisans Angkor purchases support local artisan communities directly.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Siem Reap by private charter flight or luxury vehicle transfer to Phnom Penh (approximately 1-hour flight or 6-hour scenic road journey — flight recommended for premium experience). Check in to a luxury Phnom Penh hotel (Rosewood Phnom Penh or Raffles Hotel Le Royal recommended).
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Royal Palace and Silver Pagoda complex — the official residence of King Norodom Sihamoni, featuring stunning Khmer and French colonial architecture. Admire the Throne Hall, the Napoleon III Pavilion, and the Silver Pagoda's floor of 5,000 silver tiles and its priceless Emerald Buddha. Private guided tour with a royal historian.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cruise along the Tonlé Sap and Mekong Rivers on a private luxury riverboat. Watch Phnom Penh's skyline and the confluence of four rivers (Chaktomuk) glow in the evening light. Champagne and canapés served on deck.

meals.breakfast: Final breakfast at Siem Reap boutique hotel — a leisurely spread before the transfer
meals.lunch: Lunch in Phnom Penh upon arrival at Topaz Restaurant — French-Cambodian fine dining institution beloved by diplomats and gourmands
meals.dinner: Private dinner on the riverboat cruise — curated Cambodian seafood menu with Mekong river prawns, crab, and seasonal vegetables; local Angkor craft beer and Cambodian wines

day_by_day.notes: Private charter flight between Siem Reap and Phnom Penh is approximately 45 minutes and highly recommended for comfort. Book Royal Palace tickets in advance; it closes at midday on certain days — verify schedule. Dress modestly for the Royal Palace visit.

day_by_day.morning: Sober but profoundly important historical morning: visit the Tuol Sleng Genocide Museum (S-21 Prison) — the former high school converted into a Khmer Rouge detention and torture center. A private guide will provide sensitive, expert historical context on the Cambodian genocide (1975–1979). Essential for understanding modern Cambodian history and resilience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Choeung Ek Killing Fields Memorial — a UNESCO-recognized site of remembrance approximately 15 km from the city. Spend time in reflection at the Buddhist stupa memorial. Afterward, decompress with a visit to the National Museum of Cambodia — a stunning terracotta pavilion housing the world's finest collection of Khmer sculpture and artifacts.
day_by_day.evening: Evening at leisure in Phnom Penh. Explore the vibrant riverfront promenade (Sisowath Quay). Visit the Central Market (Phsar Thmei) — a stunning 1937 Art Deco landmark — for a brief evening browse.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — extensive international and Cambodian buffet with fresh tropical juices and Cambodian egg dishes
meals.lunch: Lunch at Friends Restaurant (Phnom Penh) — a renowned social enterprise training restaurant for street youth; excellent Cambodian fusion tapas and fresh juices
meals.dinner: Dinner at Sra'y at Hotel de la Paix or Khéma Riverfront — sophisticated Phnom Penh dining with French-Khmer fusion cuisine and an exceptional cocktail program

day_by_day.notes: Tuol Sleng and Choeung Ek are emotionally intense experiences. Allow time for quiet reflection. Photography is permitted but should be done respectfully. These sites are critical to understanding Cambodia's recent history and are deeply meaningful to Cambodian people.

day_by_day.morning: Private day trip to Oudong — the former royal capital of Cambodia (pre-Phnom Penh). Visit the hilltop stupas housing the ashes of former Cambodian kings, and the beautifully restored Vipassana Dhura Buddhist Meditation Center. Enjoy panoramic views over the rice paddies and Mekong floodplain. A peaceful, rarely visited gem.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Phnom Penh. Visit Wat Phnom — the hilltop temple that gives the city its name — and the surrounding French Quarter with its elegant colonial architecture. Private walking tour of the Colonial Quarter with an architectural historian. Browse the Russian Market (Phsar Toul Tom Poung) for premium silk, silver jewelry, and antiques.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner in Phnom Penh before the journey south to the coast tomorrow.

meals.breakfast: Early hotel breakfast before departure to Oudong
meals.lunch: Traditional Cambodian lunch at a riverside restaurant in Oudong — fresh fish from the Tonlé Sap prepared in local style with rice and seasonal vegetables
meals.dinner: Farewell Phnom Penh dinner at Malis Phnom Penh — sister restaurant to the Siem Reap flagship; innovative Cambodian fine dining with a beautifully curated wine list

day_by_day.notes: Oudong is approximately 40 km north of Phnom Penh — about 1 hour by private car. Comfortable walking shoes recommended for the hilltop climb. The Russian Market is best visited in the afternoon when it is slightly less crowded.

day_by_day.morning: Private luxury transfer from Phnom Penh to Kep or Kampot on the southern coast (approximately 3–4 hours by private vehicle; scenic route through rural Cambodia). Check in to a luxury coastal property — Knai Bang Chatt in Kep (a stunning modernist boutique resort on the Gulf of Thailand) is highly recommended.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Kep National Park — a forested hilltop reserve with jungle trails, sea views, and resident monkeys. Visit the iconic Kep Crab Market — famous throughout Cambodia for its fresh blue swimming crabs cooked with Kampot pepper (one of the world's most prized peppers, grown in the nearby hills). Enjoy a leisurely afternoon on the resort's private beach or infinity pool.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails on the resort terrace overlooking the Gulf of Thailand with views toward the Vietnamese islands of Phu Quoc. The sky turns extraordinary shades of orange and pink over the calm sea.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast in Phnom Penh before departure
meals.lunch: Lunch at the Kep Crab Market — fresh steamed blue crab with green Kampot pepper sauce, grilled squid, and iced Angkor beer; a quintessential Cambodian coastal experience
meals.dinner: Dinner at Knai Bang Chatt's Le Bout du Monde restaurant — exceptional seafood and Cambodian coastal cuisine; try the Kampot pepper lobster and fresh catch of the day

day_by_day.notes: November is perfect for the Cambodian coast — dry season, calm seas, temperatures around 28–32°C. Kampot pepper is a must-buy; visit a certified pepper farm if time allows. Kep is a small, tranquil town — perfect for unwinding after the intensity of the historical sites.

day_by_day.morning: Private sunrise kayaking or stand-up paddleboarding in the calm waters of the Gulf of Thailand off Kep. Optional: a guided snorkeling trip to Rabbit Island (Koh Tonsay) — a pristine, largely undeveloped island a short boat ride from Kep with clear waters, coral, and white sand beaches. Spend the morning swimming, snorkeling, and relaxing on the island.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the resort for a final indulgent afternoon. Enjoy a signature Khmer herbal massage and spa treatment at the resort spa. Visit a Kampot pepper farm (30-minute drive) for a private guided tour of the plantation — taste and purchase premium certified Kampot pepper to take home. Final packing and preparation for departure.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell sunset dinner at the resort or at a nearby premium restaurant. Private transfer arrangements to Phnom Penh airport or onward destination as required.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely gourmet breakfast at the resort — fresh tropical fruits, Cambodian-style rice porridge, eggs Benedict, and cold-pressed juices
meals.lunch: Light beach lunch on Rabbit Island — fresh grilled fish, coconut water served in the shell, and tropical fruit
meals.dinner: Grand farewell dinner at Knai Bang Chatt — chef's special tasting menu celebrating the finest ingredients of coastal Cambodia; Kampot pepper prawns, sea bass ceviche, and mango sticky rice for dessert; paired with a selection of fine wines

day_by_day.notes: Boat to Rabbit Island takes approximately 20 minutes; departures are frequent from Kep Beach. The Kampot pepper farm visit (Sothy's Pepper Farm or La Plantation) should be booked in advance. Arrange airport transfer well in advance — Phnom Penh International Airport is approximately 3.5–4 hours from Kep. Consider an overnight in Phnom Penh if departing early the following morning.
